name: Walking calorie
seoTitle: Walking calorie Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Walking calorie: work out calories from your weight and the distance. A free sports calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Give the Walking calorie calculator your weight, the distance and the walking time and it returns calories. Think of it as a shortcut for a training session, a performance comparison or a competition result. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Walking calorie calculator work?
sections.html:
The Walking calorie calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports calories in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the sex and the slope); then you type in your weight, the distance and the walking time.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A measured quantity, entered by default in kilograms. The unit chip switches it to any of the 29 supported units.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as male and female. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 11 options, such as -5%, -4% and -3%. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilometers. The unit chip switches it to any of the 34 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in hours. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.

2 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Walking calorie calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Calories=walking time × your weight × (distance ÷ walking time, slope)
Walking speed=distance ÷ walking time
Calories=7700 × weight lost
Steps=-164042 × distance ÷ (15 × sex − 125)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.
  • Shown in kilometers per hour, and convertible to any of the 25 units on that chip.
  • Shown in kilograms, and convertible to any of the 29 units on that chip.
  • A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Length, opening in kilometers
  • Time, opening in hours
  • Speed, opening in kilometers per hour
  • Mass, opening in kilograms

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Walking calorie calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Planning a session around a target you already know
  • Tracking progress across a training block
  • Comparing two athletes or two attempts fairly
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — your weight, the distance and the walking time — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Walking calorie calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns calories, derived from your weight, the distance and the walking time. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Walking calorie calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for your weight, the distance and the walking time, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter your weight in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Your weight opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Walking calorie calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
